source.title: The Early Phase of Neural Network Training
source.authors: Jonathan Frankle; D. Schwab; Ari S. Morcos

page_placements.theme: Prior training changes subsequent memorization and transfer

record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on random labels and measures a downstream consequence for IMP subnetworks, addressing early-training data dependence rather than directly measuring random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: Random-label pretraining is an experimental condition, but the reported outcome is later IMP-subnetwork evaluation accuracy, not training error on the random labels. The paper does not report the claim's test error at chance or fitting time.
record.test_reason: The study measures how random-label pretraining affects subsequent IMP-subnetwork accuracy, not random-label fitting or memorization dynamics. This related outcome does not test V1–V6; differences in downstream trainability do not establish that real patterns are learned before noise.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label result: misleading labels prevent pretraining from approximating the early supervised state useful for IMP. The broader conclusion is that task labels are unnecessary for approximating this state, since self-supervised rotation can do so, but correct labels substantially accelerate the process.
record.recipe_differences: Studies early training through iterative magnitude pruning with rewinding and downstream subnetwork accuracy; it does not measure random-label training error, test error, or fitting time.
record.method_sensitivity: Random-label pretraining duration: up to 10 epochs yields no improvement over rewind-to-zero, while longer pretraining begins to hurt accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-20, random-label pretraining through 10 epochs does not improve subsequent IMP-subnetwork accuracy over rewinding to initialization; longer pretraining hurts accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label pretraining does not reproduce the early supervised-training state that enables accurate sparse IMP subnetworks.

record.problems: For the random-label condition, the text reports no numeric accuracy values; Figure 9 is described qualitatively. The outcome is downstream IMP-subnetwork performance, not direct random-label fitting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional random-label results are described in text with recoverable model-specific numeric values. Appendix Figure A9 shows other models' random-label conditions only in figures, without textual outcome descriptions; no separate rows were extracted from those plots.

untested.parts: Random-label training error, chance test performance, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative time to fit real versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Perfect training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test-error degradation across label-corruption fractions.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting or is necessary for true-label generalization.
The order and dynamics of learning real patterns versus memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Figure A9's additional architectures are already declared in rows_left_out and measure the same downstream outcome. Neither those results nor the self-supervised pretraining time comparison tests a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero training error and chance test error on random labels without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether the two are learned differently over training.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on CIFAR-10 with randomized labels, then used as the initialization for normal training and IMP.

conditions.value: up to 10 epochs; longer pretraining also considered

rows.measure: Evaluation accuracy of IMP-pruned subnetworks after pretraining
rows.value: Pretraining on random labels for up to 10 epochs provides no improvement above rewinding to iteration 0; longer pretraining begins to hurt accuracy.
rows.note: This measures downstream IMP-subnetwork performance, not whether the network fits the randomized training labels. The text gives no numerical accuracy for this comparison.
rows.check: The subject, baseline and qualitative outcome match Section 6.1. Specify pretraining durations as 2, 5, 10 and 40 epochs. The outcome is accuracy after subsequent true-label training and pruning, so it cannot determine any claim version.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.1; Figure 9 upper left; Section 6 experimental procedure; Table A1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study draws inspiration from random-label fitting but measures whether pretraining produces an initialization suitable for sparse-subnetwork training.

tranche.reason: Random-label pretraining is evaluated through subsequent IMP-subnetwork accuracy, a related construct that does not test V1–V6.

source_check.notes: Figure 9 lists pretraining durations of 2, 5, 10 and 40 epochs. Section 6.1 states the qualitative comparison without numerical accuracy values; this outcome does not establish random-label fitting or the learning order of signal and noise.
